extracted.intended_audience: general newspaper readers and journalists interested in wartime developments
extracted.subtask_description: Reporting and public-relations practices for military operations during wartime, describing how press corps and military public-relations staffs coordinated coverage, access, and news release policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public relations as a military operation
rubrics_metrics.description: “Public relations won't win the war, but if carried out as a military operation it can make a substantial contribution to the effort.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat PR as an operational activity integrated with military planning rather than as separate publicity; organize it with military-style command, planning, and coordination so it supports broader campaign objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assure a balanced picture of the operation
rubrics_metrics.description: “A particular effort was made to assure a balanced picture of the operation, so that no small section would get the glory for the whole occupation through a breakdown in communications or other accident.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan correspondent assignments and information flow to avoid uneven or sensationalized coverage that exaggerates any one unit's role; ensure coverage reflects the whole operation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide PR officers with advance access to combat plans
rubrics_metrics.description: “For possibly the first time, public relations officers were made privy to detailed combat plans well in advance to help them in making their arrangements.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give PR staff early, controlled access to operational plans so they can prepare logistics, embed correspondents appropriately, and coordinate releases without compromising security.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinate and manage correspondent allocation and communications
rubrics_metrics.description: “They had to compromise between a great number of newspaper men who wanted to go and the limited space available; dicker for a share of the Signal Corps’ limited communications facilities; co-ordinate London plans with those of Forces going from the United States ... and instruct a Corps of field public relations officers.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set priorities for who travels with forces, allocate scarce transport and comms resources, synchronize international press plans, and provide clear instructions to field PR personnel to manage press logistics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish a dedicated PR staff led by experienced personnel
rubrics_metrics.description: “A special staff section was set up under Major (now Lieutenant Colonel) Joseph B. Phillips ... and Major Ira Wey Porter ...”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create a specialized public-relations section and appoint leaders with professional journalism or editorial experience to plan and execute media operations effectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare and use preferential/controlled news lists for local populations
rubrics_metrics.description: “On the quiet, a preferential list of news to the [people] in North Africa.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare prioritized or controlled sets of items tailored for local audiences (and likely for security considerations), managing what information is distributed in occupied or sensitive areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withhold reporting of losses until enemy likely already knows
rubrics_metrics.description: President Roosevelt defended the administration’s policy withholding news of naval losses until it is clear that the enemy already has possession of the information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delay release of certain loss-related information for operational security and to avoid giving the enemy intelligence or causing unnecessary domestic panic; release only when it is judged that enemy acquisition or other factors make disclosure acceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep politics out of wartime reporting
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid politicizing operational reporting or using wartime news for partisan advantage; emphasize unity and operational priorities over political debate during campaigns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deploy and instruct a corps of field public-relations officers
rubrics_metrics.description: References to instructing a Corps of field public relations officers and coordinating them with headquarters plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Train and assign field PR officers to manage on-the-ground press relations, embed procedures for escorting correspondents, handling last-minute embarkation decisions, and enforcing information controls.
